effect_estimate.comment: Standardized PCA/varimax factor scores regressed via OLS with robust SEs on 2018 municipal coverage percentages (Table 4). Descriptive means across 574 municipalities (Table 2): water supply 61.608% (SD 18.512), sewerage 42.347% (SD 35.981), solid waste 47.883% (SD 39.533); 59.8% (N=456) had a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan (PMSB) and 50.9% (N=471) had a Municipal Sanitation Policy (PPSB), with chi-square tests (p < 0.05) showing lower plan/policy adoption in smaller municipalities.
effect_estimate.value: In OLS multiple linear regressions with robust standard errors (N = 391 municipalities), municipal institutional capacity factor scores significantly predicted service coverage: (1) Water supply coverage (R2 = 0.1601, F = 16.82, p = 0.000): Financial Capacity beta = 6.015 (SE = 1.020, p = 0.000), Technical Capacity beta = 2.669 (SE = 0.985, p = 0.007), Operational Capacity beta = 2.412 (SE = 0.916, p = 0.009), and Political Capacity (PMSB/PPSB planning/policy factor) beta = -1.890 (SE = 0.883, p = 0.033); (2) Sanitary sewerage coverage (R2 = 0.1933, F = 24.90, p = 0.000): Financial Capacity beta = 7.359 (SE = 1.482, p = 0.000), Technical Capacity beta = 3.941 (SE = 1.574, p = 0.013), Operational Capacity beta = 13.068 (SE = 1.650, p = 0.000), and Political Capacity beta = -0.661 (SE = 1.641, p = 0.687); (3) Solid waste collection coverage (R2 = 0.5667, F = 135.74, p = 0.000): Financial Capacity beta = 10.064 (SE = 1.413, p = 0.000), Technical Capacity beta = 2.249 (SE = 1.273, p = 0.078), Operational Capacity beta = 28.260 (SE = 1.400, p = 0.000), and Political Capacity beta = 2.555 (SE = 1.329, p = 0.055).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 19, Table 2; PDF p. 21-23, Section 4 and Table 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional observational regression of secondary municipal indicators (SNIS 2018 and IBGE 2017) documenting statistical associations between municipal institutional capacity dimensions (including statutory municipal sanitation plans/policies) and service coverage rates, without direct empirical observation of administrative plan execution or federal grant disbursement; capped by cross-sectional design ceiling and reflects documented association (1).

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines the existence of statutory Municipal Basic Sanitation Plans (PMSB) and Municipal Public Sanitation Policies (PPSB) under Law 11.445/2007 (which condition municipal eligibility for federal sanitation funds and contract validation) grouped into Political Capacity, alongside municipal technical, financial, and operational capacities and multi-level institutional fragmentation/titularity challenges under Laws 11.445/2007 and 14.026/2020.

study_design.comment: Authors describe a quantitative, descriptive study using municipal secondary data from SNIS (2018) and IBGE (2017), analyzed via chi-square and ANOVA tests, principal-component exploratory factor analysis with varimax rotation, and OLS multiple linear regression with robust standard errors.
study_design.value: Quantitative cross-sectional observational study using exploratory factor analysis (PCA with varimax rotation) and OLS multiple linear regression with robust standard errors
